verdict.rationale: Modal documents Environments, which can be created on the CLI and targeted with an `--env` flag, and objects are scoped per Environment. That gives a first-party way to stand up a separate test environment apart from production. However, the evidence never states that Environments isolate production data or describes a dev/staging versus prod workflow. Modal Sandboxes are isolated code-execution containers, not a test environment separated from production data, so they are not credited as a substitute. Missing for 10: explicit documentation that Environments isolate data and secrets from production, a documented staging/test workflow, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: New Environments can be created on the CLI:
Most CLI commands also support an `--env` flag letting you specify which Environment you intend to interact with
It’s possible to explicitly look up objects in Environments other than the Environment your App runs within
